subject: Wellscape SIG — data lifecycle & model-training evidence
messages:

Subject: Wellscape SIG: data lifecycle & training evidence request

Hi Soojin,

We’re pulling together our SIG pack and need a few specific clarifications related to data handling for Redwood Inference prior to our security review next Friday. Can you confirm the following?

1) Retention window for request/prompt logs and whether any portion is persisted beyond debugging windows.
2) Are any customer prompts or generated content ever used to train Redwood models (including for internal research or fine-tuning) unless explicitly contracted?
3) KV/prefix cache behavior — is any of that material flushed to durable storage or retained in logs?
4) Where are logs stored (S3 buckets, regions), encryption at rest, and KMS details we can provide to our security team as evidence?

If you can attach a redaction checklist and an example lifecycle policy for logs that would be very helpful. Thanks — even a short, itemized reply will work.

Best,
Alex
Head of Security Engineering
Wellscape Health
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@wellscape.health>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Wellscape SIG: data lifecycle & training evidence request

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers we can include in the SIG export; I’ve looped in David for infra/evidence files and Marissa for contract language if you need an opt-in clause. I’ll attach the checklist and lifecycle policy once David confirms paths.

1) Request/prompt logs
- Short answer: default retention is 90 days for hosted API requests (used for billing, abuse detection, and troubleshooting).
- We offer an enterprise option (Redwood Dedicated/Private) where customers can configure shorter retention or opt for no-persistence; contractual controls allow a strict 0-day retention mode for regulated customers.

2) Model training on customer data
- Default: customer content is not used to train or improve community models. We do not feed hosted customer prompts into offline model training pipelines unless a customer signs an explicit data-use agreement that permits fine-tuning or analytics.
- If a customer opts in, that process is governed by written SOW and redaction/PII filters and can be audited.

3) KV/prefix cache behavior
- KV caches (session-level caches used to accelerate decoding) are held in-memory on the serving node for the duration of an active session and are not written to durable logs. Debug traces may include ephemeral excerpts, but those are scrubbed and kept only per the retention rules above.

4) Log storage, encryption & keys
- Hosted log buckets live in us-west-2 by default (AWS S3). All logs are encrypted at rest with customer-segregated KMS keys for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted accounts use our service-managed KMS keys unless BYOK is requested.

Evidence we will provide: redaction checklist, data-flow diagram, example S3 lifecycle policy, SOC 2 report excerpt (controls around logging/retention).

Next steps: David, can you attach the redaction checklist and lifecycle policy as discussed? Marissa, flag anything in the wording that needs legal nuance for an opt-in training clause. Alex — if you want a short paragraph we can drop into the SIG answers doc, I can produce that in the next email.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@wellscape.health>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 May 2027 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Wellscape SIG: data lifecycle & training evidence request

Adding technical details and pointing to the artefacts we’ll drop in the Drive folder.

- Storage location: primary logs S3://rw-hosted-logs-usw2 (us-west-2). Dedicated customers have dedicated buckets under their account.
- Lifecycle policy: objects tagged "prompt-log" transition to GLACIER after 30 days and are deleted after 90 days by default. (Attached: s3-lifecycle-policy.txt)
- Encryption: server-side encryption with KMS (aws:kms). For hosted customers we use service-managed CMKs; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed CMKs (BYOK).
- Access controls: logs are available to on-call engineers via an RBAC controlled interface; access requires justification and is recorded in the audit log.
- Redaction & PII: we run automated redaction on detected PII (PII classification exceptions are routed to the compliance queue). Attached: redaction-checklist.pdf (example checklist we use when responding to customer requests).

Attachments I’m adding to the shared folder: redaction-checklist.pdf, s3-lifecycle-policy.txt, data-flow-diagram.png.

-David
David Kim
Technical Operations Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying items before we close the SIG section:

- When you say "debug traces may include ephemeral excerpts" can you be explicit about who can access those traces and for how long? Are engineers able to view full prompts by default?
- For the hosted default retention (90 days) — is there an option in the Console to purge a specific customer’s logs earlier, or does that require a support ticket/contract change?

If you can point me to the exact SOC 2 control identifiers that reference log retention/auditability that would also speed review. Finally — we need a one-paragraph statement for the SIG answer bank that we can include verbatim in the questionnaire.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex

Alex — pushed final artifacts to the shared folder and drafted the one-paragraph SIG-ready answer below. I’m also attaching the checklist and lifecycle policy in this thread.

[Forwarded attachments: Wellscape_SIG_answers_v1.pdf, redaction-checklist.pdf, data-flow-diagram.png, s3-lifecycle-policy.txt]

One-paragraph SIG statement (verbatim):
"Redwood Inference retains hosted request logs for up to 90 days by default for billing, abuse detection, and operational troubleshooting. KV/prefix caches are stored in-memory for active sessions only and are not written to persistent storage. Customer content is not used to train or improve Redwood models unless explicit, contractually documented opt-in is granted. Logs are encrypted at rest (AWS KMS) and subject to lifecycle policies; Dedicated and Private customers may supply their own KMS keys and custom retention settings."

Clarifications you asked for:
- Debug traces and access: debug traces that include request excerpts are strictly restricted to a small group of SRE/Infra engineers with RBAC-controlled access; access events are logged and retained per our audit retention policy (see SOC 2 control A.12.4 reference in the attached SOC 2 excerpt).
- Console purge: Hosted customers cannot self-serve purge historical logs via the Console today — purges require a support ticket and are performed under documented procedures with an audit trail. Dedicated/Private deployments can configure immediate purge via the customer admin interface.

Links to artefacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Wellscape-SIG-evidence
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/8721
